findings.statement: SCARB1 is a surface protein (CSPA high confidence) but stains at the highest level in a vital organ (adrenal gland) and its proteome tissue-specificity score is enriched there [gene=SCARB1; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; vital_organ_protein_ts_max=5.08]. Only a small share of tumour cells express it in the weakest quarter of donors, so it ranks first in the target profile but is a weak conjugate or radioligand candidate; a high ranking does not show a conjugate would work.
SCARB1 protein is higher in tumour in the confirmatory CPTAC DIA cohort, same direction and significant, so the protein change replicates.

CD70 is a surface protein with no enrichment in vital organs in the GTEx proteome and an ADC suitability rank of [gene=CD70; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; rank=3] among the genes scored. HPA staining data are not available, so safety in normal tissue is untested by immunohistochemistry; it is a known target used as a control.
CD70 was not tested in the confirmatory CPTAC cohort (too few matched pairs); this is a gap, not a failure to replicate.

CA9 is a known target with a surface call, but stains at the top level in stomach, a vital organ, and its proteome tissue-specificity flags stomach enrichment; CSPA did not observe it at the cell surface and about a quarter of tumour cells express it in the weakest quarter of donors. Gastric toxicity is the main safety concern.

CA9 expression is not associated with progression differently between atezolizumab + bevacizumab and sunitinib [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.difference_between_arms.padj=0.917]. In CheckMate-025 nivolumab versus everolimus also shows no difference [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.difference_nivolumab_vs_everolimus.padj=0.999]; CA9 is a tumour marker, not a treatment-selection marker.

CA9 is flagged as a subgroup target candidate for PBRM1 mutation (higher in mutants in CPTAC RNA and TCGA, protein difference not significant after correction) and is lower in ccB than ccA in all three datasets. It is not flagged for VHL, BAP1 or SETD2.
CA9 is attributed to tumour cells in both single-cell datasets (Li 2022 and Zhang 2021), so the cell-type call holds in a second dataset; only four paired donors back the Zhang comparison.
CA9 was not tested in the confirmatory CPTAC cohort (too few matched pairs); this is a gap, not a failure to replicate.
NNMT is attributed to tumour cells (RCC group) in both Li 2022 and Zhang 2021 with a high tumour cell share in each, so the attribution holds in a second dataset (four paired donors in Zhang).
NNMT protein is higher in tumours in the confirmatory DIA cohort with a larger fold change than discovery and a strong adjusted p-value; direction and significance replicate.

NNMT is not associated with progression in CheckMate-025 (nivolumab, everolimus, or the difference between them) or the small Choueiri cohort after correction; all adjusted p-values are high. NNMT is a tumour-intrinsic marker with a prognosis signal in TCGA, not a therapy-selection marker.
NNMT transcripts in tumours come almost entirely from non-immune cells and correlate weakly with CD8 T cells and the immune score, so it is not an infiltration artefact and not an immune target.

SLC16A3 cell attribution does not hold across datasets: dominant group is T_NK in Li 2022 (tumour share [gene=SLC16A3; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); li2022_tumour_cell_share=0.327]) but RCC in Zhang 2021 (tumour share [gene=SLC16A3; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); zhang2021_tumour_cell_share=0.809]). Its tumour-intrinsic call is therefore uncertain.
SLC16A3 protein is higher in tumours in the confirmatory cohort and its one measured phosphosite also replicates.

ENPP3 is a known conjugate target (AGS-16C3F reached phase 2) with a surface call and no vital-organ protein enrichment, but HPA staining is at the highest level in duodenum and in kidney, so on-target off-tumour kidney exposure is a concern.
ENPP3 protein is higher in tumours in the confirmatory DIA cohort with a strong adjusted p-value; it replicates.

HK2 protein does not replicate: it is not significantly changed in the confirmatory cohort and the direction is opposite to discovery (adjusted p [gene=HK2; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_padj=0.074]), despite ranking ninth in the target profile.

PPP1R1A protein loss does not reach significance in the confirmatory cohort (adjusted p [gene=PPP1R1A; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_padj=0.17], only a few pairs), although one phosphosite replicates; treat as unconfirmed.

PSAT1 protein is lower in tumours and replicates in the confirmatory cohort (log2 fold change [gene=PSAT1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-3.946]); its one discovery phosphosite did not replicate.

PSAT1 is higher in ccB than ccA in CPTAC protein, CPTAC RNA and TCGA, and higher in BAP1-mutant tumours at the RNA level but not at the protein level; it is not flagged as a subgroup target candidate.
PCK1 protein loss replicates in the confirmatory cohort and both measured phosphosites replicate, supporting a favourable-prognosis loss-of-expression marker.
SLC6A19 protein loss and all three phosphosites replicate in the confirmatory cohort, from a modest number of pairs.

FCGR3A is almost entirely made by immune cells in tumours and tracks the immune score closely, so its tumour increase reflects infiltration, not tumour-cell expression; it is a microenvironment marker and not a tumour-intrinsic target.

EPAS1 is not associated with progression differently between nivolumab and everolimus in CheckMate-025; the everolimus arm has a higher response AUC but its hazard ratio is not significant. This is a lead from one arm only.

caveats: Confirmatory cohort did not test CA9, CD70, FABP6 or DUSP9 (too few pairs); these are gaps, not failures.
No gene differs between trial arms after correction in IMmotion150 or CheckMate-025; all treatment results are leads only.
A high ADC suitability score does not show a conjugate would work; HPA staining is missing for CD70.
Single-cell replication rests on four paired Zhang donors.

CYP2J2, ANGPTL4, VWF, L1CAM, SLPI and ALDH6A1 proteins replicate in the confirmatory cohort but were not profiled for ADC, subtype or trial layers within the call budget; EPAS1 and ranking-only candidates such as PNCK, TNFAIP6 were not individually profiled.
